Operator: Good day, and welcome to the GlobalCom Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalCom Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include robust service revenue growth across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments. We are also seeing substantial growth from our fixed wireless access offerings with a significant ramp in subscribers to 1.2 million. Further, we are concentrating on optimizing our spectrum assets for higher utilization. Additionally, our fiber buildout is showing strong promise with expanded homes passed and subscriber adoption. We are also improving our subscriber acquisition costs through efficiency gains. We are strategically investing in free cash flow generation and its prudent utilization. Finally, dividend sustainability is underway and we are enhancing EBITDA margins through key drivers.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.4 billion, representing a 5.1% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.7 billion, resulting in a margin of 48.2%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $7.5 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

Let me dive deeper into our service revenue performance, which grew 5.1% year-over-year to $14.2 billion, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of expansion. This resilience highlights our disciplined execution across wireless, broadband, and enterprise amid moderating inflation, intensifying 5G competition, and rising demand for hybrid cloud-edge solutions.

Starting with wireless service revenue, up 4.2% year-over-year to $8.9 billion, outperforming the industry average of 2.8% per CTIA data. Postpaid service revenue, 78% of the segment, rose 5.1% to $6.9 billion, driven by a 2.3% ARPU increase to $52.47—our best quarterly lift in two years. This stemmed from a mix shift to premium 5G Unlimited Max plans, now 42% of postpaid base versus 31% last year, plus pricing in high-usage markets. We added 456,000 postpaid phone net adds, beating guidance, with smartphone penetration at 92%. Our 5G Standalone network covers 85% of top 100 markets after $2.4 billion mid-band C-band deployment from the 2022 FCC auction, delivering 40% lower latency and 25% higher throughput than NSA, boosting FWA to 1.2 million subscribers, up 180% year-over-year and displacing DSL in rural areas. U.S. wireless grew 4.8%, ahead of Verizon's 3.9%, via Northeast fiber-wireless convergence. In Europe, through our Vodafone JV, it was 2.9%, offset by UK 5G uptake and EE Open RAN trials cutting capex 15-20%. Postpaid phone churn at 0.76% monthly beats T-Mobile's 0.82%. For Q4, we expect 4% to 5% wireless service growth, aided by Galaxy S24 bundles and FWA targeting 2 million subs by year-end.

Broadband service revenue surged 6.8% to $3.4 billion, our fastest-growing segment, propelled by fiber rollout and multi-gig tiers. Residential broadband hit $2.7 billion, up 7.2%, with ARPU up 3.4% to $68.21 on 72% 1 Gig+ penetration. We added 512,000 fiber net adds, FTTH to 28 million locations passed, up 22% year-over-year, ahead of AT&T and on track for 35 million by 2025. XGS-PON with Nokia and Adtran delivers 8 Gbps symmetric in 15 MSAs, lifting ARPU 25% over copper. We captured 18% share in fiber markets per New Street Research, holding churn at 1.1% despite Comcast bundling pressure, backed by 92% fiber reliability. Enterprise broadband grew 5.9% on SD-WAN with Cisco Meraki for 200+ SMBs. U.S. up 7.4% in Sun Belt overbuilds; Canada via Rogers synergies up 4.2%. We're adding Wi-Fi 7 and DOCSIS 4.0 against Starlink. Q4 guidance: 7% to 8% growth, 550,000 fiber adds.

Enterprise service revenue rose a solid 3.5% to $1.9 billion, better than Lumen's decline or Cogent's modest gain, in a cautious IT spend environment. Wireless enterprise jumped 8.2% on IoT/MEC, with private 5G for Ford and P&G at $250 million, up 35%, using CBRS and EdgeZone with AWS Outposts. Wireline/managed services up 2.1% on dark fiber and NFV via VMware telco cloud, cutting provisioning 60%. Wins: $500 million SD-WAN with a Big Four bank for SASE, Disney CDN expansions. ARPU steady at $1,450 monthly, 85% margins on software shift. North America 75% of growth at 4.1%; APAC via Singtel up 1.8% on 5G slicing. EMEA sales cycles elongated but 98% renewals, 15% cross-sell. Q4: 4% growth, slicing to 20% revenue by FY25.

Overall, service revenue gained from 1.8pp ARPU expansion and 2.4 million mobility/broadband adds, offset by 0.9pp legacy runoff. Our Converged Fabric strategy added 300bps margin accretion. We're gaining 5G coverage per Forbes and fiber density per UBS. Risks: FCC Title II, Dish buildout. FY24 service growth now +5.0% from +4.5%; Q4 +5.2%. With $7.5 billion FCF, ready for 2025 auctions, edge AI M&A.

Turning to dividend sustainability and shareholder returns, a key focus for investors. Our Board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.52 per share, up 3.4% year-over-year, our 18th consecutive hike, annualizing to $6.08 per share at 5.2% forward yield—above peer 4.1% average for AT&T, Verizon, Comcast. Five-year CAGR 6.2%, beating inflation and S&P Comm Services.

Free cash flow coverage is strong: Q3 $2.8 billion FCF, up 12% year-over-year, FY24 guide $11.5-12.0 billion, up 9%. Covers $7.2 billion dividend at 1.65x, target 1.5-1.8x; payout 62% vs. Charter 75%, Vodafone 80%+. Capex $8.2 billion or 18% revenue: 55% 5G SA/Open RAN (15% capex save), 25% fiber (5 million new U.S. premises), 20% content like NBA MaxStream deal boosting ARPU 8% to $14.50.

North America 55% FCF, 450,000 postpaid adds on 5G Ultra Wideband (85% footprint); Europe 30%, 42% margins in UK/Germany via Vodafone JV ($1.2 billion savings); APAC 15%, up 22% on 5G mmWave, 12% enterprise edge share. Net debt/EBITDA 2.6x from 2.8x via $3.5 billion monetizations (towers to American Tower, data centers to Digital Realty), A- rating, low costs on $2 billion green bonds.

YTD returns $9.8 billion: $5.4 billion dividends, $4.4 billion buybacks (4.2% shares at $112, 7% EPS accretion), 8.7% yield topping Comcast 7.2%. New program mid-2024, 3-4% yields. Network + Content flywheel bundles 5G/MaxStream for 15% ARPU; AI slicing with Unity/Epic for $2 billion enterprise by 2026; hybrid model limits video churn to 1.2% vs. Dish 2.5%.

Our dividend is solid, backed by FCF, leverage, 5G/fiber/content. Committed to 5%+ growth, 9-11% returns.

On free cash flow generation and utilization, Q3 $2.8 billion, up 15% year-over-year and 8% sequential, YTD $8.1 billion toward $11-12 billion FY24 guide, ahead of consensus post-5G buildout. Operating cash $4.5 billion up 12%, from 2.1 million postpaid adds on Unlimited Max (25% ARPU), 550,000 fiber adds (45% U.S. market), NexaStream $1.2 billion up 22% on content/ads (RPM +18%). Capex $1.7 billion or 22% revenue, down 5%, via Open RAN (30% sites, 15-20% save), cloud-native 5G SA, moderating C-band amortization $400 million.

North America 75% FCF at $2.1 billion up 18% ($52.50 ARPU, suburban fiber); Europe 15% $420 million (copper shutdowns $150 million opex); APAC 10% $280 million (spectrum sharing). Utilization: 60-70% returns, dividends $1.2 billion ($0.65/share, 28th hike, 4.2% yield), repurchases $800 million (12 million shares at $68, 3% EPS), debt paydown $500 million (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x), reinvest $300 million (LATAM content $150 million, AWS edge $100 million).

Q4 $3.0-3.2 billion, FY capex low $7.0-7.5 billion (10-15% efficiency). Funds content inflation, FWA (800,000 YTD), AI orchestration (-20bps churn), European fiber M&A for 45% margins.

Subscriber acquisition cost trends improved: blended SAC $385 per postpaid, down 9% sequential from $422, 18% year-over-year from $470, low end of guide. Wireless $410 down 8%, streaming $295 down 12%. North America $372 (digital 65%, Apple/Samsung bundles <$250 devices); LATAM $520 (eSIM/influencers); EMEA $445 (fiber/streaming bundles).

Drivers: NovaAI platform +28% conversions ($18 CPI), bundling (35% uptake, $220 SAC), churn-linked commissions (LTV:CAC 3.2x). Q4 $375-390; sub-$350 FY26 vs. Verizon $450+, Comcast $420+.

Spectrum assets utilization at 78% average, up from 68%, with 1.2 GHz total: 160 MHz low-band (85% utilized for coverage), 620 MHz mid-band (82%, 5G SA 55% sites, DSS 25% efficiency, 450 Mbps), 420 MHz mmWave (62%, sub-5ms). Northeast 84%, Southeast 72%, Europe JV 75%. +22% efficiency via Open RAN 2,500 sites. Demand: FWA 40% more spectrum, media 35% bits.

Plans: optimize (80 MHz refarm, DSA CBRS $200 million revenue); acquire (Auction 110 $2.5-3 billion 100-140 MHz, DISH lease 60 MHz); innovate (6G OAM, NTN Starlink, wholesale slicing). Supports 20-25% wireless EBITDA CAGR.

Fiber buildout: Q3 4,200 route miles (YTD 7,800, FY 16-17k), XGS-PON 42% COs (10G symmetric, 450 Mbps usage). Capex $1.2 billion, $28/foot. Homes passed 8.7 million (+32% YoY, 1.9 million YTD), to 11.5-12 million YE. Southeast 680k (2.1 million total), Midwest 520k (1.9M, BEAD $450M), West 410k (1.1M), Northeast 290k (1.8M).

Subscribers 3.2 million (+48% YoY, 420k adds), take rate 36.8% (+420bps, 52% greenfield), ARPU $112 (+14%, 62% 1G+), churn 0.9%. 65% residential, 20% SMB, 15% MDU. Cross-sell mobile 22%, ecosystem $168. FY adds 1.6-1.8M, 42% IRR.

EBITDA margin 48.2%, up from prior via mix (Connectivity 68%, wireless +7% $4.2B ARPU $52.40, broadband +5% $3.1B DOCSIS 4.0), efficiencies ($250M savings, Open RAN 18%, AI chatbots 22%, content $80M save). North America 41.2%, Europe 32%, APAC 28%. H2 +100-150bps: FWA 40% margins, TeleStream 35% pen, edge 55%+, hedges. Headwinds: interconnect +10%, content. 3-5% annual accretion to 2026.

Lisa Patel: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage to 85% of top markets and increasing capacity with C-band and Open RAN deployments across 2,500 sites. We're investing in network slicing and edge computing for IoT, AR/VR, and low-latency media delivery. Network uptime remains at 99.999%, with spectral efficiency up 22% year-over-year. We are also improving fiber integration for converged backhaul.

David Kim: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth with postpaid adds exceeding 450,000 and improved satisfaction scores at NPS 74 for fiber. Bundled offerings like 5G with streaming resonate, delivering seamless experiences. Digital channels now 65% of acquisitions, boosting cross-sell to 35%. We are also focused on lowering SAC through AI personalization and retention-linked incentives.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are driving innovation with AI and machine learning for network automation and efficiency gains of 20%. We're developing 5G FWA, private networks, and 6G R&D including OAM multiplexing. Our R&D centers on edge AI with AWS, NTN integration, and Wi-Fi 7 for future-proofing services.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding private 5G networks and edge computing?

David Kim: Good morning, John. Thanks for the question. In enterprise, we're leveraging our private 5G networks and EdgeZone platform, generating $250 million this quarter, up 35% year-over-year, with wins like Ford, P&G, and a Big Four bank's $500 million SD-WAN SASE contract. Our CBRS and AWS Outposts integrations deliver low-latency MEC, securing 8.2% wireless enterprise growth. We're competing by offering 55%+ margins on software-centric services, 98% renewals, and 15% cross-sell, ramping slicing to 20% revenue by FY25. This positions us ahead in IoT and media CDN peering with Disney.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding free cash flow and capex allocation?

Michael Chen: Hi Jane. Inflation and rates are headwinds, but our $2.8 billion Q3 FCF up 15% and FY $11-12 billion guide provide buffer. We're mitigating via Open RAN efficiencies (15-20% capex save), copper shutdowns ($150 million opex), and hedges on energy/chips. Capex down 5% to 22% revenue despite 5G, with deleveraging to 2.3x net debt/EBITDA via prepays and monetizations. Shareholder returns prioritized at 60-70% FCF: dividends, buybacks 3% EPS, tuck-ins like LATAM content. This sustains 1.65x dividend coverage amid macro.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing fiber efficiencies and network decommissioning?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core, with initiatives like Open RAN reducing site energy 18%, legacy 4G/3G decommissioning (15% small cells, 80 MHz refarm), and green bonds for fiber/5G builds. Fiber efficiencies—XGS-PON 42% COs, micro-trenching—cut deployment costs 18%, payback 28 months, while 92% reliability lowers churn-driven energy. We're measuring via EBITDA-to-FCF conversion at 48%, carbon intensity per TB down 20%, and BEAD grants for unserved areas. Success ties to 45% margins long-term, aligning growth with ESG.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in GlobalCom Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
